correctness.rationale: For real finite-dimensional l_p with p>1, strict convexity yields a unique weighted p-mean root and derivative. For p>2, normalization of signed p-1 moments and a two-sided dual inequality show that no residual distribution exceeds the best two-index tangent; opposite-sign two-supported residuals attain this derivative. For p<2 and support k>=3, positive-gradient bounds give V/min v, a smooth monotone regularization proves a global Lipschitz estimate across zero residuals, and near-zero residuals at a minimum-weight coordinate attain the limiting derivative. The support-one/two and Hilbert cases are direct, and equality in Holder classifies nonexpansivity. The standalone checker exercises 108000 random moment-constrained samples and prescribed sharp limits; no finite test is used as a universal proof.

value.rationale: A uniform formula for every weighted real line supplies sharp constants beyond previous coarse finite-atomic bounds and beyond the covered equal-weight special case. The pair-support extremal principle above p=2, minimum-weight sensitivity below p=2, and complete nonexpansivity rigidity expose an exact structural phase diagram directly relevant to best approximation stability, not an arbitrary slice or a mere symbolic renaming.
